adaptation: Newton v1.7.0 finite ALM and legacy hard-contact equations. Three-dimensional hard contacts use fresh surface anchors, midpoint matching and force transport. Joint-adjacent contacts retain numerical patch rho separately from point-force correspondence. Structured components use Newton color assembly/commit with project contact and LRC conflict edges; free components keep Giles descending GS. Free hard contacts retain Newton legacy alpha 0.95, shared rho, projected Coulomb duals and its positive tangent metric. Project CPU assembly expands simultaneous normal/tangent metrics as rho I and isotropic world inertia as its diagonal. Four-point reduction applies to structured and zero-gravity patches; gravity free patches retain the Giles boundary. Geometry gap choices, interior witnesses, SCA release and CPU adjacency ownership are mapped in References/Newton.md.

Original AVBD hard-row laws and step scheduling with project collision pruning, positive angular curvature bounds, current-point residuals and LRC hooks. Planar hard-contact blocks and duals use the Newton shared-rho policy; project pressure conditioning, world-plane normal bounds, batched assembly and support-geometry cache remain inside the original body-block iteration. Ownership: References/Newton.md.

Giles AVBD hard joints and their paired contact discretization, inertia and velocity. Newton geometry, history and structured color scheduling enter the same primal/dual loop. Project numerical patch-rho retention, 1 cm structural shape gaps and source-attributed C0 bias enter contact initialization. Batched joint/contact equations, lower-triangle assembly, typed adjacency and single-copy support data are CPU implementation choices. Stage ownership: References/Newton.md.
Y-up to Z-up; PyramidDemo retains 20 rows and uses 2 of 40 copies; FrictionDemo keeps all 100 boxes and maps product material coefficients to geometric-mean coefficients.

Y-up to Z-up; original dimensions, density, arrangement and counts; sharp AVBD boxes and hard contacts; floor 400 x 400 m. FrictionTest includes the 11-box 45-degree ramp and 11-box continuous-impulse cases; the shared continuous-impulse input uses the initial yaw's world direction for 360 steps.

Depth-adaptive normal C0 stabilization from Solver::computeC0 in this open-source research fork. Upstream fade thresholds are 50 and 200 mm; the project selects 1 and 5 mm for its contact accuracy.
